curiosities: Its chips were designed by Jay Miner's team, who went on to design the Amiga's.
Its ANTIC graphics chip runs a 'display list', a small program describing each line of the screen.
Star Raiders, a first-person space game, was one of its showcase titles.
Its POKEY sound chip was also used in many Atari arcade machines.
Its processor is a 6502 at 1.79 MHz.
The Atari 400 has a flat membrane keyboard.
The XL range followed in 1983 and the XE range in 1985.
Its SIO port chains disk drives and printers together; Joe Decuir, who worked on it, later worked on USB.
M.U.L.E. first came out on it in 1983.
Boulder Dash began on it in 1984.
Lucasfilm's Ballblazer and Rescue on Fractalus! were made for it.
